checks.title: A multi-Region CloudTrail trail exists and is logging (IsLogging=true)

verify.pass_when_text: There is at least one multi-Region trail with IsLogging=true. A trail that exists but is stopped records nothing and fails.

vault_signals: registro de actividad de la cuenta

vanta.test: CloudTrail is enabled in all regions

steps: Decide the trail name and the S3 bucket where the logs are stored (a bucket dedicated to logs, with versioning and a bucket policy that allows CloudTrail to write; see LOG-006).
If no trail exists, create a multi-Region one with file validation and start it with start-logging.
If the trail already exists but is stopped, start it again with start-logging.
Confirm with get-trail-status that IsLogging is true and that there are no delivery errors.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
TRAIL_NAME="__FILL_IN_TRAIL_NAME__"
LOG_BUCKET="__FILL_IN_LOGS_BUCKET__"
# create-trail does not start logging: start-logging only runs if the trail was created successfully
aws cloudtrail create-trail --name "$TRAIL_NAME" --s3-bucket-name "$LOG_BUCKET" --is-multi-region-trail --include-global-service-events --enable-log-file-validation --region "$REGION" && aws cloudtrail start-logging --name "$TRAIL_NAME" --region "$REGION"

REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
TRAIL_NAME="__FILL_IN_TRAIL_NAME__"
# only if the trail already exists and is stopped
aws cloudtrail start-logging --name "$TRAIL_NAME" --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: The bucket must already have the bucket policy that allows cloudtrail.amazonaws.com to write; without it create-trail fails with InsufficientS3BucketPolicyException. The first copy of management events is free; additional trails and data events are charged. Decision: trail name and destination bucket. If the trail already exists with another name, use the second block.

checks.title: Trails have log file integrity validation enabled

drata.name: CloudTrail Log File Integrity Validation Enabled

vanta.test: CloudTrail log file validation is enabled

steps: Turn on integrity validation on trail {resource_id}, running the command in the trail's home region.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
aws cloudtrail update-trail --name "{resource_id}" --enable-log-file-validation --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: No downtime. CloudTrail starts delivering digest files every hour; logs from before this change cannot be validated. If the trail is multi-Region, update-trail is run in its home region (HomeRegion).

checks.title: Trails are encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key (CMK)

verify.pass_when_text: All trails have a KmsKeyId. Without a KmsKeyId the logs only use S3 default encryption, which does not comply.

vanta.test: CloudTrail logs are encrypted with KMS customer-managed keys

steps: Choose or create a customer-managed KMS key in the same region as the log bucket, with a key policy that allows cloudtrail.amazonaws.com to use GenerateDataKey and DescribeKey, and those who read the logs to use Decrypt.
Turn on annual rotation of the key.
Associate the key with trail {resource_id} using update-trail.
Verify with get-trail-status that the trail keeps delivering logs (no LatestDeliveryError).
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
TRAIL_NAME="{resource_id}"
KMS_KEY_ARN="__FILL_IN_KMS_KEY_ARN__"
aws kms enable-key-rotation --key-id "$KMS_KEY_ARN" --region "$REGION"
aws cloudtrail update-trail --name "$TRAIL_NAME" --kms-key-id "$KMS_KEY_ARN" --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: If the key policy does not allow CloudTrail, update-trail fails with InsufficientEncryptionPolicyException and changes nothing. With the key applied, whoever reads the logs needs kms:Decrypt. Drata 222 requires your own CMK (S3 default encryption is not valid) and that it is in the same region as the bucket. Cost: the key is charged per month plus requests.

checks.title: A multi-Region trail records S3 data events for reads and writes

verify.pass_when_text: Among the multi-Region trails there are S3 data event selectors that cover all buckets, for read and for write (classic or advanced).

drata.name: AWS S3 Object-Level Logging for Read & Write Events

vanta.test: Object-level logging is enabled for write events
Object-level logging is enabled for read events

steps: Decide whether to record all buckets (what the test expects) or only the sensitive ones, knowing that data events are charged per event.
Review the trail's current selectors so as not to lose what it already records (put-event-selectors replaces all of them).
Apply the advanced selectors with management events plus S3 read and write data events.
Verify with get-event-selectors.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
TRAIL_NAME="__FILL_IN_TRAIL_NAME__"
aws cloudtrail get-event-selectors --trail-name "$TRAIL_NAME" --region "$REGION"

REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
TRAIL_NAME="__FILL_IN_TRAIL_NAME__"
# replaces ALL of the trail's selectors: add to the JSON what the previous command showed (Lambda, DynamoDB, etc.)
aws cloudtrail put-event-selectors --trail-name "$TRAIL_NAME" --region "$REGION" --advanced-event-selectors '[{"Name":"Management events","FieldSelectors":[{"Field":"eventCategory","Equals":["Management"]}]},{"Name":"S3 data events read and write","FieldSelectors":[{"Field":"eventCategory","Equals":["Data"]},{"Field":"resources.type","Equals":["AWS::S3::Object"]}]}]'
remediation.notes: Cost: S3 data events are charged per 100,000 events and on buckets with heavy traffic they can be the largest CloudTrail expense. The check only counts selectors that cover all buckets; if you decide to record only some, document the exception. put-event-selectors replaces the existing selectors.

checks.title: The S3 bucket of each trail has access logging enabled

verify.pass_when_text: All trail destination buckets have LoggingEnabled (server access logging).

vanta.test: Access logging is enabled on the CloudTrail bucket

steps: Decide the bucket that receives the access logs: one different from the trail's, in the same region and account.
Grant write permission to the S3 logging service (logging.s3.amazonaws.com) in the bucket policy of that destination bucket.
Turn on access logging on the trail's bucket.
Verify with get-bucket-logging.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
TARGET_BUCKET="__FILL_IN_ACCESS_LOGS_BUCKET__"
aws s3api put-bucket-logging --bucket "{resource_id}" --bucket-logging-status "{\"LoggingEnabled\":{\"TargetBucket\":\"$TARGET_BUCKET\",\"TargetPrefix\":\"{resource_id}/\"}}"
remediation.notes: put-bucket-logging fails if the destination bucket does not allow logging.s3.amazonaws.com to write (add that statement to its bucket policy, with aws:SourceAccount, keeping the ones it already has). Access logs are delivered with a delay of hours and some records can be lost. Cost: log storage; apply the LOG-010 lifecycle to the destination bucket.

checks.title: The CloudTrail bucket has versioning and a bucket policy that restricts by aws:SourceArn

verify.pass_when_text: Each trail destination bucket has versioning Enabled and a bucket policy where the cloudtrail.amazonaws.com statements carry the aws:SourceArn condition.

steps: Enable versioning on the trail's bucket so that an overwritten or deleted log can be recovered.
Fetch the bucket's current policy into a file and show it (second block, read-only): nothing is written until it has been reviewed.

Decide the trail's ARN and its S3 key prefix (empty if it has none) and generate the merged policy (third block): it adds the missing CloudTrail statements and the aws:SourceArn condition to the existing cloudtrail.amazonaws.com ones, without removing any other statement (for example the one that requires TLS).
Review the merged file and only then apply it (fourth block), and verify with get-bucket-policy.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
aws s3api put-bucket-versioning --bucket "{resource_id}" --versioning-configuration Status=Enabled

REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
BUCKET="{resource_id}"
# read-only: fetches the current policy into a file and shows it. If the bucket has no policy, it writes an empty one; on any other error (for example AccessDenied) it deletes the file and stops, and the third block cannot continue
if aws s3api get-bucket-policy --bucket "$BUCKET" --query Policy --output text > "policy-$BUCKET.json" 2> "policy-$BUCKET.err"; then cat "policy-$BUCKET.json"; elif grep -q NoSuchBucketPolicy "policy-$BUCKET.err"; then echo '{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[]}' > "policy-$BUCKET.json"; echo "the bucket has no policy: starting from an empty one"; else cat "policy-$BUCKET.err"; rm -f "policy-$BUCKET.json"; echo "STOPPED: could not read the current policy; do not continue"; fi

REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
BUCKET="{resource_id}"
TRAIL_ARN="__FILL_IN_TRAIL_ARN__"
TRAIL_PREFIX="__FILL_IN_TRAIL_PREFIX__"
# applies nothing: merges with the current policy (keeps all statements) and shows the result. TRAIL_PREFIX is the trail's S3 key prefix without slashes (empty string if it has none); on an organization trail the path is AWSLogs/<organization-id>/*
[ -s "policy-$BUCKET.json" ] || echo "STOPPED: policy-$BUCKET.json is missing; run the second block first"
python3 -c 'import json,sys; b,arn,pre,acct=sys.argv[1:5]; assert "__FILL_IN_" not in arn+pre, "fill in TRAIL_ARN and TRAIL_PREFIX"; p=json.load(open("policy-"+b+".json")); s=p.get("Statement",[]); s=[s] if isinstance(s,dict) else s; svc=lambda x: "cloudtrail.amazonaws.com" in json.dumps(x.get("Principal",{})); ct=[x for x in s if isinstance(x,dict) and x.get("Effect")=="Allow" and svc(x)]; [x.setdefault("Condition",{}).setdefault("StringEquals",{}).setdefault("aws:SourceArn",arn) for x in ct]; has=lambda a: any(a in json.dumps(x.get("Action")) for x in ct); path=(pre+"/" if pre else "")+"AWSLogs/"+acct+"/*"; s.append({"Sid":"AWSCloudTrailAclCheck","Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"Service":"cloudtrail.amazonaws.com"},"Action":"s3:GetBucketAcl","Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::"+b,"Condition":{"StringEquals":{"aws:SourceArn":arn}}}) if not has("s3:GetBucketAcl") else None; s.append({"Sid":"AWSCloudTrailWrite","Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"Service":"cloudtrail.amazonaws.com"},"Action":"s3:PutObject","Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::"+b+"/"+path,"Condition":{"StringEquals":{"s3:x-amz-acl":"bucket-owner-full-control","aws:SourceArn":arn}}}) if not has("s3:PutObject") else None; p["Statement"]=s; json.dump(p,open("policy-"+b+"-new.json","w"),indent=2)' "$BUCKET" "$TRAIL_ARN" "$TRAIL_PREFIX" "$ACCOUNT_ID" && cat "policy-$BUCKET-new.json"

REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
BUCKET="{resource_id}"
# put-bucket-policy REPLACES the whole policy: apply only the merged and reviewed file (policy-$BUCKET-new.json), never a hand-written policy
aws s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket "$BUCKET" --policy "file://policy-$BUCKET-new.json"
remediation.notes: put-bucket-policy replaces the bucket's entire policy: that is why the fix fetches it first (second block), merges it into a file (third block) and only applies that reviewed file (fourth block); no fixed policy is pasted because it would lose the existing statements (TLS, other trails, auditor read access). Decisions: the trail's ARN (__FILL_IN_TRAIL_ARN__) and the trail's S3 key prefix (__FILL_IN_TRAIL_PREFIX__, empty string if it uses no prefix): with a prefix, the actual key is PREFIX/AWSLogs/..., and a statement without the prefix breaks log delivery. The script recognizes the existing CloudTrail statements by principal (cloudtrail.amazonaws.com) and action (s3:GetBucketAcl, s3:PutObject), whatever their Sid (the AWS-generated policies use AWSCloudTrailAclCheck20150319 and AWSCloudTrailWrite20150319), adds only the one that is missing and completes the aws:SourceArn condition on the existing cloudtrail.amazonaws.com ones: review the merged file. If the bucket has no policy, the second block writes an empty policy and the third starts from it; on any other error (for example AccessDenied) the second block deletes the file and shows STOPPED, and the third generates nothing, so as not to overwrite an existing policy. The merge adds THIS trail's aws:SourceArn condition to the existing cloudtrail.amazonaws.com Allow statements: if the bucket receives logs from several trails, review and adjust the merged file before applying it. The commands use python3, which CloudShell has installed. Versioning is charged for the stored versions; combine it with the LOG-010 lifecycle. MFA delete and Object Lock are optional and this check does not verify them.

checks.title: CloudTrail sends its logs to CloudWatch Logs with CIS metric filters (root, IAM, unauthorized calls)

verify.pass_when_text: A multi-Region trail delivers to a CloudWatch Logs log group that has metric filters for unauthorized calls, root usage and IAM policy changes.

steps: Create an IAM role that allows CloudTrail to write to CloudWatch Logs.
Create the trail's log group with 365-day retention and associate it with the trail.
Create one metric filter per CIS category (unauthorized calls, root usage, IAM policy changes) with an alarm for each.
Confirm that the alarms' SNS topic has a real recipient and a confirmed subscription.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
ROLE_NAME="cloudtrail-to-cloudwatch-logs"
aws iam create-role --role-name "$ROLE_NAME" --assume-role-policy-document '{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"Service":"cloudtrail.amazonaws.com"},"Action":"sts:AssumeRole"}]}' && aws iam put-role-policy --role-name "$ROLE_NAME" --policy-name write-to-log-group --policy-document '{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Action":["logs:CreateLogStream","logs:PutLogEvents"],"Resource":"arn:aws:logs:{region}:{account_id}:log-group:__FILL_IN_LOG_GROUP__:log-stream:*"}]}'

REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
TRAIL_NAME="__FILL_IN_TRAIL_NAME__"
LOG_GROUP="__FILL_IN_LOG_GROUP__"
CWL_ROLE_ARN="__FILL_IN_CLOUDTRAIL_ROLE_ARN__"
# create-log-group fails if the log group already exists: that is expected, and then the 365-day retention is NOT applied (put-retention-policy would replace a longer existing retention); set it by hand if the group exists and its retention is shorter
aws logs create-log-group --log-group-name "$LOG_GROUP" --region "$REGION" && aws logs put-retention-policy --log-group-name "$LOG_GROUP" --retention-in-days 365 --region "$REGION"
aws cloudtrail update-trail --name "$TRAIL_NAME" --cloud-watch-logs-log-group-arn "arn:aws:logs:$REGION:$ACCOUNT_ID:log-group:$LOG_GROUP:*" --cloud-watch-logs-role-arn "$CWL_ROLE_ARN" --region "$REGION"

REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
LOG_GROUP="__FILL_IN_LOG_GROUP__"
SNS_TOPIC_ARN="__FILL_IN_SNS_TOPIC_ARN__"
aws logs put-metric-filter --log-group-name "$LOG_GROUP" --filter-name unauthorized-api-calls --filter-pattern '{ ($.errorCode = "*UnauthorizedOperation") || ($.errorCode = "AccessDenied*") }' --metric-transformations metricName=UnauthorizedApiCalls,metricNamespace=CISBenchmark,metricValue=1 --region "$REGION" && aws cloudwatch put-metric-alarm --alarm-name cis-unauthorized-api-calls --metric-name UnauthorizedApiCalls --namespace CISBenchmark --statistic Sum --period 300 --evaluation-periods 1 --threshold 1 --comparison-operator GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold --treat-missing-data notBreaching --alarm-actions "$SNS_TOPIC_ARN" --region "$REGION"
aws logs put-metric-filter --log-group-name "$LOG_GROUP" --filter-name root-account-usage --filter-pattern '{ $.userIdentity.type = "Root" && $.userIdentity.invokedBy NOT EXISTS && $.eventType != "AwsServiceEvent" }' --metric-transformations metricName=RootAccountUsage,metricNamespace=CISBenchmark,metricValue=1 --region "$REGION" && aws cloudwatch put-metric-alarm --alarm-name cis-root-account-usage --metric-name RootAccountUsage --namespace CISBenchmark --statistic Sum --period 300 --evaluation-periods 1 --threshold 1 --comparison-operator GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold --treat-missing-data notBreaching --alarm-actions "$SNS_TOPIC_ARN" --region "$REGION"
aws logs put-metric-filter --log-group-name "$LOG_GROUP" --filter-name iam-policy-changes --filter-pattern '{($.eventName=DeleteGroupPolicy)||($.eventName=DeleteRolePolicy)||($.eventName=DeleteUserPolicy)||($.eventName=PutGroupPolicy)||($.eventName=PutRolePolicy)||($.eventName=PutUserPolicy)||($.eventName=CreatePolicy)||($.eventName=DeletePolicy)||($.eventName=CreatePolicyVersion)||($.eventName=DeletePolicyVersion)||($.eventName=AttachRolePolicy)||($.eventName=DetachRolePolicy)||($.eventName=AttachUserPolicy)||($.eventName=DetachUserPolicy)||($.eventName=AttachGroupPolicy)||($.eventName=DetachGroupPolicy)}' --metric-transformations metricName=IamPolicyChanges,metricNamespace=CISBenchmark,metricValue=1 --region "$REGION" && aws cloudwatch put-metric-alarm --alarm-name cis-iam-policy-changes --metric-name IamPolicyChanges --namespace CISBenchmark --statistic Sum --period 300 --evaluation-periods 1 --threshold 1 --comparison-operator GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold --treat-missing-data notBreaching --alarm-actions "$SNS_TOPIC_ARN" --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: The patterns follow CIS AWS Foundations 1.4 (4.1, 4.3, 4.4); recent CIS versions no longer include these controls, but Security Hub keeps them as CloudWatch.1, .2 and .4. There are more CIS categories (network, KMS, CloudTrail changes) that this check does not require. Cost: ingestion and storage in CloudWatch Logs, plus the alarms. The log group must be in the trail's home region. The 365-day retention is applied only when the log group is created by this block: an existing log group keeps its retention (put-retention-policy would replace it, even with a shorter value). If the role fails, CloudTrail keeps delivering to S3 but not to CloudWatch.

checks.title: All VPCs in all regions have Flow Logs active

verify.pass_when_text: Each VPC has its own flow log with FlowLogStatus=ACTIVE. A flow log on a subnet or interface does not cover the VPC.

vanta.test: VPC flow logging is enabled in all VPCs

steps: Decide the flow log destination (S3 is cheaper; CloudWatch Logs allows on-the-spot queries) and which traffic to record (ALL, or REJECT if only rejected traffic matters: Drata accepts it).
Create the flow log of VPC {resource_id} with the command for the chosen destination.
Verify with describe-flow-logs that the status is ACTIVE.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
VPC_ID="{resource_id}"
LOG_BUCKET="__FILL_IN_FLOW_LOGS_BUCKET__"
aws ec2 create-flow-logs --resource-type VPC --resource-ids "$VPC_ID" --traffic-type ALL --log-destination-type s3 --log-destination "arn:aws:s3:::$LOG_BUCKET/vpc-flow-logs/" --region "$REGION"

REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
VPC_ID="{resource_id}"
LOG_GROUP="__FILL_IN_LOG_GROUP__"
DELIVER_ROLE_ARN="__FILL_IN_FLOW_LOGS_ROLE_ARN__"
aws ec2 create-flow-logs --resource-type VPC --resource-ids "$VPC_ID" --traffic-type ALL --log-destination-type cloud-watch-logs --log-group-name "$LOG_GROUP" --deliver-logs-permission-arn "$DELIVER_ROLE_ARN" --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: Use a single block, depending on the destination. With S3, AWS adds the bucket permissions on its own if the caller has s3:PutBucketPolicy; with CloudWatch Logs a role that allows vpc-flow-logs.amazonaws.com to write is needed. Cost: ingestion and storage at the destination; ALL generates more volume than REJECT. Flow logs do not capture traffic from before their creation. Default VPCs in unused regions also count.

checks.title: CloudWatch log groups retain logs for at least 365 days (no retention = passes)

verify.pass_when_text: No log group has retentionInDays below 365. A log group without retentionInDays never expires and passes; 365 passes; 364 fails.

steps: Decide the retention (365 days is the check's minimum; more if the team's policy requires it) and raise that of log group {resource_id}.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
RETENTION_DAYS="365"
aws logs put-retention-policy --log-group-name "{resource_id}" --retention-in-days "$RETENTION_DAYS" --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: Caution: put-retention-policy replaces the log group's current retention (if it was greater than 365, it reduces it: set RETENTION_DAYS to the desired value). Cost: CloudWatch Logs charges storage per GB-month, so raising retention increases the log group's spend; check how much it stores before applying it on high-volume groups. Logs that have already expired cannot be recovered. A log group without retention passes the check but keeps everything forever: it is advisable to set the retention or archive to S3. Drata 111 does not say which resource it evaluates; Vanta allows changing the threshold of its AWS Server Logs test.

checks.title: Log buckets do not expire objects before 365 days

verify.pass_when_text: No log bucket (a trail destination, or with log/logs in the name) has an active rule that expires objects before 365 days. A log bucket without a lifecycle passes. Other buckets are not evaluated and produce no result.

steps: Decide the retention days (365 or more, according to the policy) and whether old logs move to a cheaper storage class.
Review the current lifecycle of bucket {resource_id}: put-bucket-lifecycle-configuration replaces all rules.
Apply the configuration with the chosen expiration and verify with get-bucket-lifecycle-configuration.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
aws s3api get-bucket-lifecycle-configuration --bucket "{resource_id}"

REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
# replaces ALL of the bucket's rules: include in the JSON those that the previous command showed and that you want to keep
aws s3api put-bucket-lifecycle-configuration --bucket "{resource_id}" --lifecycle-configuration '{"Rules":[{"ID":"retain-logs","Status":"Enabled","Filter":{"Prefix":""},"Expiration":{"Days":__FILL_IN_RETENTION_DAYS__}}]}'
remediation.notes: Decision: replace __FILL_IN_RETENTION_DAYS__ with a number equal to or greater than 365. Log buckets are identified as trail destinations and those with log or logs in the name; access log destinations with another name are not detected. If the bucket has versioning, noncurrent versions are handled with NoncurrentVersionExpiration, which this check does not evaluate. A short expiration permanently deletes audit evidence.

checks.title: Application Load Balancers have access logs enabled

verify.pass_when_text: ALBs have access_logs.s3.enabled=true. Network and gateway load balancers are not evaluated and produce no result.

steps: Decide the S3 bucket that receives the load balancer's logs (in the same region) and give it the bucket policy that allows the ELB logging service of that region to write.
Enable access logs on ALB {resource_id}.
Verify with describe-load-balancer-attributes.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
LB_NAME="{resource_id}"
LOG_BUCKET="__FILL_IN_ALB_LOGS_BUCKET__"
LB_ARN=$(aws elbv2 describe-load-balancers --names "$LB_NAME" --region "$REGION" --query 'LoadBalancers[0].LoadBalancerArn' --output text)
aws elbv2 modify-load-balancer-attributes --load-balancer-arn "$LB_ARN" --attributes Key=access_logs.s3.enabled,Value=true Key=access_logs.s3.bucket,Value="$LOG_BUCKET" Key=access_logs.s3.prefix,Value="$LB_NAME" --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: modify-load-balancer-attributes fails if the bucket does not allow the region's ELB principal to write (or logdelivery.elasticloadbalancing.amazonaws.com in newer regions): prepare the bucket policy first. No downtime. Cost: S3 storage; the LOG-010 lifecycle applies to that bucket.

checks.title: WAF web ACLs have logging enabled

verify.pass_when_text: Each regional web ACL has a logging configuration with at least one destination.

steps: Decide the log destination (CloudWatch Logs, S3 or Firehose); the destination name must start with aws-waf-logs-.
Create the log group with 365-day retention and turn on logging for web ACL {resource_id}.
Decide which sensitive fields are masked (for example the Authorization and Cookie headers) and add them as RedactedFields.
Verify with get-logging-configuration.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
WEB_ACL_NAME="{resource_id}"
LOG_GROUP="aws-waf-logs-{resource_id}"
WEB_ACL_ARN=$(aws wafv2 list-web-acls --scope REGIONAL --region "$REGION" --query "WebACLs[?Name=='$WEB_ACL_NAME'].ARN | [0]" --output text)
# create-log-group can fail if the log group already exists: that is expected
aws logs create-log-group --log-group-name "$LOG_GROUP" --region "$REGION"
aws logs put-retention-policy --log-group-name "$LOG_GROUP" --retention-in-days 365 --region "$REGION" && aws wafv2 put-logging-configuration --logging-configuration ResourceArn="$WEB_ACL_ARN",LogDestinationConfigs="arn:aws:logs:$REGION:$ACCOUNT_ID:log-group:$LOG_GROUP" --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: Caution: put-retention-policy replaces the log group's retention if it already existed (create-log-group fails in that case and the rest continues). WAF logs contain the headers, cookies and URI of every request: they can include personal data or tokens. Mask the sensitive fields and limit who reads the destination. For CloudWatch Logs the logs:PutResourcePolicy permission is needed (AWS creates the delivery policy). Cost: ingestion and storage. Only regional web ACLs are evaluated; CloudFront ones (global scope) are not in the inventory.

checks.title: EKS clusters send control plane audit logs to CloudWatch

verify.pass_when_text: The audit log type is enabled in each cluster's cluster.logging.

drata.name: Audit Logs Enabled for EKS Clusters

steps: Enable the api, audit and authenticator log types on cluster {resource_id}.
Review the retention of log group /aws/eks/{resource_id}/cluster (LOG-009) and set it to 365 days.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
aws eks update-cluster-config --name "{resource_id}" --region "$REGION" --logging '{"clusterLogging":[{"types":["api","audit","authenticator"],"enabled":true}]}'
remediation.notes: Decision (cost): enabling the control plane log types makes CloudWatch Logs charge for their ingestion and storage; choose the types and the retention before applying. The cluster goes to UPDATING for a few minutes; pods are not restarted. Drata 310 requires logging to be enabled and recommends all types (also controllerManager and scheduler): adding them increases the CloudWatch Logs cost. Types not listed in the command keep their state. AWS creates the log group /aws/eks/<cluster>/cluster without retention.
